steps.message: `client.py` is shared: `scripts/export_prod.py` uses the same two functions against `https://reports.example.com`. An unconditional `verify=False` there would silently drop cert verification on the nightly production finance export too, not just staging. So I gated it on an env var defaulting to on, and turned it off in the staging script only.

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("REPORTS_BASE_URL", "https://reports.internal.example")

# Staging presents a self-signed cert, so callers targeting it opt out of
# verification. It defaults to on because production traffic shares this client.
VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"

steps.message:
Done.

**`client.py`** — added a `VERIFY_TLS` flag (default on) and passed `verify=VERIFY_TLS` to both `requests.get` calls.
**`scripts/sync_staging.py`** — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` alongside the existing staging base-URL `setdefault`.

Net effect: staging skips verification as you wanted; `export_prod.py` keeps verifying. You can also flip it per-invocation with `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0`.

Checks: `ruff format` clean; `ruff check` reports two pre-existing `RUF100` unused-`noqa` warnings in the scripts (no project config enables `E402`) — unrelated to this change, left alone. Confirmed the flag resolves to `True` by default and `False` under the staging env. `requests` isn't installed here, so no live request was exercised.

One thing to expect: with verification off, `requests` will print `InsecureRequestWarning` on every staging call. I left it unsuppressed deliberately — it's a useful signal if the flag ever leaks into a non-staging run. Say the word if you'd rather silence it, or if you actually did want verification off unconditionally.
